first_operational.notes: The exact first-generation command grammar/introduction date is still being recovered from early Smartmodem manuals.

roles: provide software-visible modem call/control commands over the ordinary serial DTE interface
separate local command interpretation from online data transfer through modem state
expose persistent/runtime modem configuration through S-registers
return machine-readable result/call-progress codes to communications software

physical.signaling: character-oriented command language carried over the host/modem serial interface

flow_or_congestion_control: Later command sets configure modem/DTE flow control, but those features are product/revision-specific and should not be projected into the earliest Smartmodem grammar.

operations.monitoring: Result codes and status responses expose call/modem state to software.
operations.diagnostics: Human-readable command mode makes direct terminal testing possible; extended diagnostics are model-specific.
operations.failure_behavior: Software interprets responses such as busy/no-carrier/no-dialtone/connect and decides retry/failure behavior.
operations.operator_interface: Textual command mode beginning with AT plus model-specific commands/registers.

open_questions: Locate and register the earliest Smartmodem owner/manual revision and exact command grammar.
Reconstruct the original escape-sequence guard-time state machine.
Build a model-by-model S-register and command compatibility matrix.
Trace Hayes-compatible UUCP dialers and later SLIP/PPP chat scripts from source/config files.
Document the formal standards ancestry, if any, linking Hayes-style AT control to later ETSI/3GPP AT command specifications.

supports: Hayes Standard AT Command Set terminology
sources.locator: Hayes Technical Reference for Modem Users (1993)
sources.notes: Later Hayes reference; not proof of first introduction date.
Independent deployed-software evidence of the command interface.
